## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is the port-0 ephemeral-bind workflow specified end-to-end — acceptor binds port 0, reads back the OS-assigned port via `fixpp_session_acceptor_bound_endpoint`, initiator dials that port? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005/§US2 AC3] — PASS: US2 AC3: "Given an acceptor bound on port 0, When `fixpp_session_acceptor_bound_endpoint` is called on a bound acceptor, Then a non-zero OS-assigned port is returned"; FR-005 specifies the complete workflow; quickstart.md lines 53-55 demonstrate the full sequence: `fixpp_engine_start`, then poll `fixpp_session_acceptor_bound_endpoint` until port != 0, then create initiator with that port. End-to-end specified.
- [x] CHK007 Is the not-yet-bound poll semantics (`*port_out = 0` + `FIXPP_ERR_OK` until the accept loop has run a step) specified so the consumer knows to poll, not to treat 0 as an error? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005/§Edge Cases] — PASS: FR-005 states "a not-yet-bound session yields `*port_out = 0` with `FIXPP_ERR_OK` so the consumer can poll"; Edge Cases: "not-yet-bound (port 0); the consumer polls (quickstart while-loop pattern, not an error)"; quickstart.md: `while (port == 0) fixpp_session_acceptor_bound_endpoint(acc_s, &port)`. The poll-not-error semantics is unambiguous.
- [x] CHK008 Is the `reset_seqnum_policy` production default (`bilateral_strict`) and the purpose of pinning the setter (a deterministic SC-001 ABI surface at the freeze) documented? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005b/§Clarifications] — PASS: FR-005b states "the session-config surface must expose it explicitly before the `0→1` freeze, so the SC-001 round-trip exercises it"; Clarifications section D-4 documents "production default = `bilateral_strict`" and "7 symbols, no +1 contingency"; research.md D-4: "reset-policy setter pinned (it's a config surface that MUST be exercised at the freeze)". The purpose and the default are documented.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality (Measurability)

- [x] CHK009 Is the D-4 establishment requirement framed as an EMPIRICAL-FIRST acceptance — a fresh `bilateral_strict` pair with both-side `set_reset_on_logon(true)` MUST establish through the public C-ABI — rather than an assumed-true precondition? - [x] CHK010 Is the LENIENT fallback specified as a WITNESSED path (never silently waived) if strict establishment fails, so the requirement has a defined failure-handling branch? [Coverage, Spec §Clarifications (kickoff Q design)/§FR-005b] — PASS: Clarifications D-4: "fallback if `bilateral_strict` + `reset_on_logon(true)` does NOT establish: pivot to `bilateral_lenient` (WITNESSED, never waived)"; FR-005b closes "LENIENT is a witnessed fallback if strict does not establish — never silently waived". The failure branch is defined and the requirement is that it is witnessed, not waived.

[Measurability, Spec §SC-001/§US2 AC4] — PASS: US2 AC4: "Using `FIXPP_SECURITY_INSECURE_PLAIN_TCP` over loopback (`127.0.0.1`)"; SC-001: "plaintext-TCP loopback (`127.0.0.1`)"; quickstart.md uses `"127.0.0.1"` for both acceptor bind and initiator dial.
